text:
incidents-bot: Pager: high CPU + tail latency on inference pool `us-west-2/g4dn` (alert: pod_cpu_util > 90% for 5m). Triggered @maya @ryan-oncall

maya (SRE): seeing a big spike coincident with traffic surge from a handful of API keys. Latency p50->p95 jump. Customers reporting timeouts.

ryan-oncall: I'll take. tagging runtime infra. What's the customer impact? Any paid enterprise tenants?

liam (runtime): quick look — sustained token throughput increased ~3x on a subset of routes (chat/generation). Continuous batching got large batch sizes, queue depth high, NVidia kernels overloaded. Some requests hit 30s tail.

sasha (prod-eng): Customer impact: two mid-market customers reported failures in last 10m, one internal smoke test also failed. No full outage but elevated error rate.

maya (SRE): initial mitigation plan: 1) throttle suspect API keys to 20rps 2) reduce max_batch_latency_ms to trade throughput for latency 3) temporarily disable long-running streaming feature on the impacted pool 4) on-call handoff if this goes > 30m

liam (runtime): agree. propose specific batching changes: set `max_batch_latency_ms=25` (was 100), `min_batch_size=1` (was 8), `max_batch_size=64` (was 512), and enable `reject_large_batches=true` to force per-request low-latency paths. This will reduce throughput but should pull p95 down quickly.

maya (SRE): execute order: throttle -> batching change -> feature disable. I'll push throttles first so we don't overload during the config change.

maya (SRE): throttling keys now: calling internal admin api.

maya (SRE): command run:
```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/keys/throttle -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"keys": ["cust-452","cust-310"], "rps": 20, "reason": "live-mitigation batch overload"}'
```

deploy-bot: Throttle jobs queued: job id job_2026_1851 queued by maya.

liam (runtime): confirmed throttle accepted. Observability: per-key qps dropping now. Good.

liam (runtime): applying batching config change to us-west-2 pool. Pushing a runtime config patch; this is hot-reloadable.

liam (runtime): patch body:
```json
{
  "pool": "us-west-2/g4dn",
  "batching": {
    "max_batch_latency_ms": 25,
    "min_batch_size": 1,
    "max_batch_size": 64,
    "reject_large_batches": true,
    "continuous_batching": true
  }
}
```

liam (runtime): api call:
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://controlplane.internal/v1/pools/us-west-2/g4dn/config -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CTRL' -d @patch.json
```

deploy-bot: Config patch applied (rolling), rollout id rollout_452. Changes will hit nodes in ~30s.

sasha (prod-eng): heads-up: this will increase per-token cost and drop throughput. Customer-facing note? We should send a brief incident banner.

maya (SRE): monitoring p95/P99.

(30s)

liam (runtime): p95 improved from ~3.2s to ~600ms on the affected pool. CPU utilization dropping to 65%. Some throughput loss as expected.

ryan-oncall: status update to paging: "Mitigation in progress: throttled heavy keys and reduced batch latency. Latency improving; continuing to monitor. ETA 15m to confirm stability."

sasha (prod-eng): posting customer banner now: short note about degraded performance on certain generation routes and that we're throttling to protect availability. :warning:

maya (SRE): next step — long tail due to streaming sessions. Recommend disabling streaming for the pool for 10 minutes while we confirm. Anyone object?

liam (runtime): ok from me. toggle streaming flag: `streaming_enabled=false` on pool. Hot-reload too.

liam (runtime): command:
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://controlplane.internal/v1/pools/us-west-2/g4dn/config -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CTRL' -d '{"streaming_enabled": false}'
```

deploy-bot: Streaming toggle applied, rollout id rollout_453.

maya (SRE): monitoring... error rate dropped from 6%->1.2%. Latency stable.

ryan-oncall: handing off to maya for next hour — heading to incident overlap meeting. @maya you're owner.

maya (SRE): taking the page. I'll keep this thread updated and escalate if anything regresses.

liam (runtime): post-mitigation notes for root cause investigation: batch sizing heuristics let continuous batching grow too large under skewed routing; internal backpressure thresholds didn't kick soon enough. We'll add an automated ramp-down policy to cap batch growth when CPU>80% for 1m.

sasha (prod-eng): action items: 1) ops to confirm customer throttle durations and whether we should issue temporary quota credits 2) runtime to implement automatic batch-shed policy 3) comms to customers affected (already posted) 4) follow-up postmortem.

maya (SRE): logging all action items in the incident ticket. For immediate customer relief, can we offer an emergency quota bump for one impacted enterprise tenant?

liam (runtime): yes — will coordinate with sales to approve. I can temporarily exempt `cust-452` from the 20rps cap if they confirm paying enterprise.

maya (SRE): will keep throttle in place for 30m then reassess. If stability holds we'll gradually relax `max_batch_latency_ms` back to 50 then 100 over a couple hours.

ryan-oncall: FYI for post-incident: consider adding a canary config that applies conservative batching to 10% of traffic when new continuous batching heuristics are deployed.

sasha (prod-eng): noted. I'll own the canary design with liam.

maya (SRE): final status (12m from start): latency and errors within acceptable range. Mitigations remain in place. Creating follow-up doc for postmortem + timeframe to re-enable streaming.

incidents-bot: Incident recorded: incident_2026_1851 - severity: P2 - mitigated but under monitoring. Owner: maya (SRE).

maya (SRE): thanks team. I'll hand off final watch to night SRE at 1840 UTC and update ticket.

liam (runtime): quick note to include in postmortem: sample config for auto-ramp policy we discussed:
```yaml
batch_shedding:
  enabled: true
  cpu_threshold_percent: 80
  lookback_seconds: 60
  target_max_batch_size: 128
  ramp_down_factor: 0.5
```

sasha (prod-eng): good. postmortem draft assigned to me.

maya (SRE): closing thread for active coordination. Will reopen if any regression. :white_check_mark:
